title: Full AES-128 known-key tuple distinguisher, Gilbert 2014

target.description: Full standard AES-128 with its real known master key and key schedule. Section 4.2 first presents independent subkeys, then explicitly applies the same construction to standard AES-128 on printed p.221.

setting.key_relation: A single known AES-128 key. The independent-subkey case motivates the proof but is not substituted for the standard-key-schedule instance recorded here.
setting.key_population: every known AES-128 key in the source construction
setting.reference_model: A perfect random 128-bit permutation and inverse with q<=N=2^64 queries. Proposition 6 gives an upper bound 2^256*(5^16/(2^128-(N-5)))^3, approximately 2^-16.5, for obtaining the same existential relation R.
assumptions: Known-key structural model, not the unknown-key encryption-security experiment.
The tuple relation quantifies over two 128-bit constants: after the specified outer AES transformations, byte-position distributions are uniform.
The relation is checked without supplying the true key to the checker; its description nevertheless involves AES round operations.
The source distinguishes mathematical construction validity from the interpretive question of how meaningful this relation is under the standard key schedule.
PDF19 verifies the existential relation using eight 32-bit frequency tables and a second pass over candidate row constants; auxiliary table size is not total attack peak memory.

time.note: Section 4.2 gives T=N=2^64 to construct the tuple, and describes a relation check below the same AES-equivalent work scale; this is a source-level cost estimate. The source uses an AES-equivalent dominant-work estimate; tuple derivation and relation verification are not assumed to be identical machine operations.

data.note: Order N of the produced relation, not a sample requirement on an unknown secret-key oracle.

memory.note: No explicit peak-memory estimate is extracted; intermediate frequency tables do not justify guessing a total storage exponent.

preprocessing.note: No separately reusable preprocessing budget is reported.

success.description: For every known key in the stated instance, Algorithm A deterministically constructs the complete source-defined tuple satisfying relation R. This is a theoretical construction guarantee, not secret-key recovery or an experimentally measured fraction. The ideal-permutation construction bound is a separate event.

review.scope: Targeted verification of Properties 1–2 and Algorithm A, the exact relation and applicable key model; the independent-key and standard-schedule targets stay separate.

components.description: Proposition 6 bounds ideal-permutation relation construction for q <= N = 2^64 queries, approximately 2^-16.5. It is not an AES-side recovery probability.

evidence.locator: Printed pp.203-204, Section 2; pp.208-210, Section 3; pp.217-219, Section 4.2, algorithm A, relation R, efficient checking and Proposition 6; p.221, application to AES10.
evidence.interpretation: The result is explicitly applicable to the real full AES-128 but assumes its key is known. The source's discussion of relation meaningfulness is retained; no unknown-key break or security-bit reduction is inferred.

evidence.locator: Complete PDF1–23 / printed200–222; Definitions1–2 PDF9–10; §4.1 PDF14–17; §4.2 PDF18–22; allreferences.
evidence.interpretation: Complete exact conference-version inventory. Ideal-permutation success bounds, tuple order and AES-side deterministic construction remain distinct.

evidence.locator: PDF4/printed203 footnote2; PDF18–22/printed217–221 Section4.2, Algorithm A, Proposition6 and unmodified standard-AES applicability.
evidence.interpretation: Success backfill: source-proved real-cipher relation construction and ideal-world probability bound are distinct events. No new attack, resource conversion or whole-paper audit.

limitations: The full-round label describes the primitive instance, not practical key recovery.
The paper's relation is more intricate than the eight-round relation; the full-AES discussion does not give the same key-non-encoding argument as the independent-subkey variant.
Bounded later-literature check identifies GR17 and its revised-description note; its full result inventory is a separate work, not a cost replacement for this relation.
PDF21 lists K6..K11 in one discussion sentence although the ten-round definition has K0..K10; round count follows the explicit definition, not that local index typo.
